subtitle: "Body composition and activity levels across demographic groups"
---

```{python}
#| echo: false
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "docs/assets")
from portal_helpers import load, fig_defaults, kpi_row, data_note, COLORS

import pandas as pd

data = load("bmi_activity")
```

Body Mass Index and physical activity are key modifiable health determinants.
The CanHealth 2024 survey collected self-reported height and weight (for BMI calculation)
and weekly physical activity levels.

---

::: {.section-header}
## BMI distribution
*Histogram of individual-level BMI values (kg/m²)*
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
hist = pd.DataFrame(data["bmi_histogram"])

# Reference lines for WHO BMI classifications
bmi_zones = [
    (0,   18.5, "rgba(91,147,191,0.08)", "Underweight"),
    (18.5, 25,  "rgba(46,139,87,0.08)",  "Normal"),
    (25,   30,  "rgba(230,168,23,0.08)", "Overweight"),
    (30,   55,  "rgba(192,57,43,0.08)",  "Obese"),
]

fig = go.Figure()

# Shaded zones
for lo, hi, clr, label in bmi_zones:
    fig.add_vrect(x0=lo, x1=hi, fillcolor=clr, line_width=0,
                  annotation_text=label, annotation_position="top left",
                  annotation_font_size=11)

# Bars
fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
    x=hist["bin_start"] + 1.25,  # centre of 2.5-wide bin
    y=hist["n"],
    width=2.3,
    marker_color=COLORS["primary"],
    hovertemplate="BMI ~%{x:.1f}: %{y} respondents<extra></extra>",
))

fig.update_layout(
    xaxis_title="BMI (kg/m²)",
    yaxis_title="Number of respondents",
    bargap=0.05,
)
fig_defaults(fig, "BMI Distribution — All Respondents", height=420).show()
```

---

::: {.section-header}
## Mean BMI by age group and gender
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
by_demo = pd.DataFrame(data["bmi_by_demo"])
age_groups = sorted(by_demo["age_group"].unique().tolist())

fig = go.Figure()
for gender, clr in [("Man", COLORS["primary"]), ("Woman", COLORS["danger"])]:
    subset = by_demo[by_demo["gender"] == gender]
    vals   = []
    for ag in age_groups:
        row = subset[subset["age_group"] == ag]
        vals.append(float(row["mean_bmi"].values[0]) if len(row) else None)
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=age_groups, y=vals,
        mode="lines+markers",
        name=gender,
        line=dict(color=clr, width=2.5),
        marker=dict(size=8),
        hovertemplate=f"{gender}: %{{y:.1f}}<extra></extra>",
    ))

fig.update_layout(yaxis_title="Mean BMI", xaxis_title="Age group", yaxis_range=[23, 32])
fig_defaults(fig, "Mean BMI by Age Group and Gender", height=380).show()
```

---

::: {.section-header}
## Physical activity by income bracket
*Lower income is associated with lower physical activity levels*
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
pa_df = pd.DataFrame(data["pa_distribution"])
income_cats = ["Under $30K", "$30K–$59K", "$60K–$99K", "$100K–$149K", "$150K+"]
pa_levels   = [
    "Sedentary (< 30 min/week)",
    "Low (30–149 min/week)",
    "Moderate (150–299 min/week)",
    "High (300+ min/week)",
]
pa_colors = [COLORS["danger"], COLORS["warning"], COLORS["secondary"], COLORS["success"]]

fig = go.Figure()
for pa, clr in zip(pa_levels, pa_colors):
    subset = pa_df[pa_df["physical_activity"] == pa]
    vals = []
    for inc in income_cats:
        row = subset[subset["income_bracket"] == inc]
        vals.append(float(row["pct"].values[0]) if len(row) else 0)
    fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
        name=pa, x=income_cats, y=vals,
        marker_color=clr,
    ))

fig.update_layout(
    barmode="stack",
    yaxis_title="% of income group",
    xaxis_title="Household income",
)
fig_defaults(fig, "Physical Activity Levels by Income Bracket", height=430).show()
```

---

::: {.section-header}
## Statistical test: does physical activity predict BMI?
*One-way ANOVA (pingouin)*
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
anova = data["bmi_activity_anova"]
from IPython.display import display, HTML
display(HTML(f"""
<div class="stat-callout">
  One-way ANOVA: <strong>F = {anova['F']:.3f}</strong>, 
  p = {anova['p_value']:.4f},
  η² = {anova['eta_sq']:.4f} 
  ({'small' if anova['eta_sq'] < 0.06 else 'medium' if anova['eta_sq'] < 0.14 else 'large'} effect size).
  Physical activity group is a statistically significant predictor of BMI.
</div>"""))
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
data_note("BMI was calculated from self-reported height and weight, which is subject to social desirability bias in survey settings.")
```
